text:
maria: quick flag question — I'm seeing odd routing: console shows a 10% canary for /api/generate but a user hit the v1 path 100% of the time. who owns the final split?

aj: can you paste the request headers and which environment? dev/prod?

maria: prod, us-west. no special headers. console shows route rollout 10% -> v2, default v1. feature-flag service returns true for the user on "use_v2" for some traffic tests. behavior seems nondeterministic.

sam: this keeps coming up. we don't have a single-source-of-truth for "effective traffic" — console rollout vs feature flags vs runtime overrides. docs are vague.

kevin: current code path (short): feature-flag evaluation happens during auth stage, we attach a header X-RW-FF:use_v2=true. routing layer then evaluates rollout policies and runtime overrides. but there's also a per-request header X-Redwood-Rollout that can forcibly pin traffic. so precedence today ends up being: explicit runtime header > feature-flag header > rollout policy. not great.

linda: that precedence isn't obvious to users. proposal: show an "effective config" in the console and API (same data) that displays which rule won and why. also need audit logs: who toggled the flag, policy, or runtime override.

maria: +1 on the effective config. also we need telemetry traces that tag which rule matched for every request (so we can aggregate). "matched_rule: feature_flag:use_v2" etc.

aj: idea for a simple, explicit precedence we can ship quickly:

```
1. Explicit runtime override (header: X-Redwood-Rollout or route param)
2. Route-level rollout policy from API config (console-defined traffic splits)
3. Account-level feature flags (featureflag service evaluated before routing)
4. Global defaults (console/global)
```

aj: but note: if a feature-flag is used as a "guard" (i.e., opt-in gating) rather than a split decision, it should short-circuit routing and treat non-members as 0% for the feature. we need to express guard vs split semantics in the flag metadata.

sam: agree — two separate primitives: "guards" (boolean, canary gate) and "splits" (percentage traffic). currently flags are trying to be both. that causes confusion.

kevin: implementation concerns: changing evaluation order will impact running experiments. minimal approach: keep current behavior but make it explicit in runtime and console UI. then add a migration path where console can opt into the new precedence for a route (feature flag first vs route policy first).

linda: UX for rollout creation: add a checkbox "Feature flag can override this rollout" and an explainer tooltip. console should show the effective % per user segment with a "why" link that expands to show evaluation stack.

rollout-bot: Canary started — route=/api/generate, model=v2, splits=10%, initiated-by=@kevin, rollout-id=rb-2026-03-08-12

maria: action items: (1) kevin capture current code path and add a diagram in the infra docs, (2) aj draft a precedence RFC and example API schema for "guard" vs "split", (3) linda mock up console effective-config UI, (4) sam add telemetry span tags for matched_rule. I'll collect and we can sync on Thurs. :thumbsup:

aj: will do RFC. sample API snippet I'd include in RFC:

```
rollout_rules:
  - id: route-policy-1
    type: split
    variants: [{v1:90},{v2:10}]
    precedence: 2
  - id: guard-flag-1
    type: guard
    flag: use_v2
    precedence: 1
```

kevin: thanks — let's also add a migration note: changing precedence can break experiments; default to opt-in change.

linda: I'll prototype the effective-config panel and include a small timeline showing last toggles + who.

maria: perfect. if anyone hits reproducible traffic mismatches, drop logs and sample request IDs here and I'll triage.

sam: tagging @eng-sre for any infra-level tracing help.

kevin: fyi i've opened a tiny PR that logs matched_rule at debug level: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rw-inference/pull/6879 — feedback welcome.

maria: thanks all. meeting Thurs to align. :calendar:
